residencyRequirements.description: At least one party must have been a bona fide resident of Mississippi for at least six (6) months immediately preceding the filing of the complaint.

exceptions: No waiting period for fault-based divorce
waitingPeriod.description: For irreconcilable differences (no-fault) divorce, a 60-day waiting period from filing applies. No waiting period for fault-based grounds. Miss. Code §93-5-2.

noFault.name: Irreconcilable Differences
noFault.description: The parties have irreconcilable differences. Requires consent of both parties or a 60-day waiting period.

fault.name: Habitual Drug Use
fault.description: Habitual and excessive use of opium, morphine, or other such drug

fault.name: Imprisonment
fault.description: Sentenced to imprisonment in a state or federal penal institution

fault.name: Desertion
fault.description: Willful, continued, and obstinate desertion for one year

fault.name: Insanity or Idiocy
fault.description: Insanity or idiocy at time of marriage, unknown to complainant

fault.name: Pregnancy by Another
fault.description: Wife was pregnant at time of marriage by another person, without knowledge of the husband

fault.name: Incest
fault.description: Parties are within the prohibited degrees of kindred

fault.name: Bigamy
fault.description: A former marriage undissolved at time of present marriage

fault.name: Incurable Insanity
fault.description: Incurable insanity at the time of filing, after confinement for three years

groundsForDissolution.notes: Mississippi has both fault and no-fault grounds. The no-fault ground (irreconcilable differences) requires consent of both parties or a 60-day waiting period. Fault-based divorce has no waiting period.

propertyDivision.description: Mississippi uses equitable distribution with a dual classification system. The court first classifies property as marital or separate, then equitably divides marital property. Factors include: substantial contribution to the accumulation of property, use of marital property for non-marital purposes, dissipation of assets, market and emotional value of property, and the needs of each party.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Mississippi distinguishes between marital and separate property. Separate property includes property owned before the marriage, property acquired by gift or inheritance, and property excluded by agreement. Separate property is not subject to division unless commingled.

filingFees.notes: Mississippi filing fees are approximately $148 (uncontested) to $158 (contested) but may vary by county. Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals via an In Forma Pauperis motion.

basic.name: Financial Statement (Rule 8.05)
basic.description: Mandatory disclosure of income, assets, and debts per Uniform Chancery Court Rule 8.05

basic.name: Final Judgment of Divorce
basic.description: Final court order granting the divorce

service.name: Summons
service.description: Service on defendant via sheriff, process server, or certified mail
alternatives: Waiver of Service and Entry of Appearance

service.name: Waiver of Service and Entry of Appearance
service.description: Defendant voluntarily waives service and enters an appearance
service.notes: Must be signed by defendant and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Child Support Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per Mississippi Child Support Guidelines (Miss. Code §43-19-101 et seq.)

withChildren.name: Child Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Mississippi Rules of Civil Procedure and Uniform Chancery Court Rules

inState.description: Defendant must file a response within 30 days of service

outOfState.description: Defendant served outside Mississippi must file a response within 30 days of service

childSupportGuidelines.description: Mississippi uses a percentage-of-income model. Child support is calculated as a percentage of the non-custodial parent's adjusted gross income per the Mississippi Child Support Guidelines.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if application would be unjust. The percentage formula is 14% for one child, 20% for two, 22% for three, 24% for four, 26% for five or more.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Mississippi provides several types of alimony: (1) Periodic alimony — ongoing payments based on need and ability to pay, (2) Lump-sum alimony — single payment or fixed total, (3) Rehabilitative alimony — temporary support to allow a spouse to become self-supporting. The court considers the income and expenses of each party, the health and earning capacities, the needs of each party, the obligations and assets of each party, the length of the marriage, the age of the parties, and the standard of living during the marriage.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: Alimony is available to either spouse based on need and the other's ability to pay. It is more common in longer marriages.

court.name: Chancery Court
court.description: Divorce cases in Mississippi are filed in the Chancery Court (not Circuit Court). Mississippi is unique in using Chancery Court for domestic relations matters.
